notes.title: Raf Simons
notes.body: The Belgian designer whose adidas line made the chunky Ozweego runner a fashion staple. He opens the song in a pair.

notes.title: Genovese crime family
notes.body: One of the Five Families of the New York Mafia, known for keeping its business quiet. Secrecy is the family code.

notes.title: Money Trees
notes.body: Kendrick Lamar's 2012 song with Jay Rock from good kid, m.A.A.d city, about wanting to sit in the shade of a tree that grows cash. He's already there.

notes.title: Yeezus
notes.body: Kanye West's 2013 album. One of its centerpieces samples Nina Simone's Strange Fruit, and that song's title finishes the line, tying back to the trees before it.
Tea means gossip two lines earlier. Here it turns into a tee, the stained vintage T-shirt he's wearing.

notes.title: Kirby
notes.body: Nintendo's pink hero, who swallows enemies whole to copy their powers.
Floating is the Wavy persona in one word: water, ease, never fighting the rhythm. The hook repeats it until the song does what it says.

notes.title: Joe Biden
notes.body: When this came out in August 2020, Biden was days from accepting the Democratic nomination for president, and his gaffes were a running joke. A quote nobody can place gets pinned on him.

notes.title: King Midas
notes.body: The king from Greek myth who turned everything he touched into gold.
To dash is to run off fast, and a dash is also a punctuation mark, which is why a hyphen follows it.

notes.title: Raven
notes.body: The quiet, hooded member of the Teen Titans in the Cartoon Network series. With a hood up, he's her.

notes.title: Tetris
notes.body: The 1984 falling-block puzzle game where every piece has to slot into place.
The last verse is a run of puns built on a puzzle game, a cartoon detective and a sitcom. It ends on pride in being Black.

notes.title: Inspector Gadget
notes.body: The 1980s cartoon detective with a tool for every situation. His name is split across two lines.

notes.title: Arrested Development
notes.body: The Fox sitcom about the Bluth family, which shares its name with a 90s hip-hop group. He turns the title into an arrest.

notes.title: Pain 1993
notes.body: Drake's song with Playboi Carti from Dark Lane Demo Tapes, out in May 2020, a few months before this one.

notes.title: Ocean Drive
notes.body: The Art Deco strip along South Beach in Miami Beach, lined with neon-lit hotels. It's the trip he wants to take with her.

notes.title: Shy Guy
notes.body: The masked, robed enemy from Nintendo's Mario games. Covered up and quiet, he's playing one.

notes.title: Casper the Friendly Ghost
notes.body: The friendly ghost from the classic cartoons and the 1995 movie. In his love life, the women end up ghosting him.
This is the first time he draws the line on record between being an artist and being boxed in as a rap act. It's a stance he's held since, from directing his own visuals to claiming R&B as his lane.

notes.title: Toronto Raptors
notes.body: Toronto's NBA team. Drake nicknamed the city the 6, which makes six the Raptors' number too.

notes.title: Tiger Woods
notes.body: The golf great, whose last name is the joke. Woods are golf clubs and wood is also slang for an erection, and Topgolf, the driving range chain, finishes it.

notes.title: Norway
notes.body: Said out loud, the country sounds like no way. The trip she wants and the love she never had for him come down to the same answer.

notes.title: Dwyane Wade
notes.body: The Miami Heat legend wore number 3 through all three of the team's championships. He picks three as his favorite, and in Florida that number belongs to Wade.

notes.title: Yak
notes.body: Slang for cognac, Hennessy above all.
He says he had no heart at all, a store dummy, until love brought the feeling back. It's the turn the whole song hangs on.
The ending is gracious. He wishes her the best with the man she's with now and goes out on the image he started with, time standing still.
